query: What is the default policy for resummerize and concept-summary refresh in v0.25?

recall_results.summary: v0.23.0 release notes state [resummerize].enabled = false by default; operator must opt in before any LLM rewrite is attempted.
v0.24.0 release notes describe ARS Capability A as opt-in via [ars].concept_summary_enabled, mirroring the v0.23 resummerize default-off pattern.
v0.25.0 release notes explicitly preserve all v0.23 and v0.24 default-off settings; the recall_synthesis_enabled flag also defaults to false.
An older v0.23 brainstorm doc proposed making resummerize default-on once eval cleared; the proposal never landed and the production default stayed off through v0.24 and v0.25.

query: Should LongMemEval be the primary signal for whether v0.25 ships?

recall_results.summary: An early devlog argued LongMemEval should remain the north-star metric for any new search-pipeline work because v0.9.0 used it.
The v0.23 eval design doc replaced LongMemEval with a paired McNemar test on production-fixture corpora because LongMemEval mixes too many subsystems to attribute a single change.
v0.24 ship notes confirm the McNemar paired test is now the gating signal for the resummerize and concept-summary features; LongMemEval is reduced to a quarterly regression check.
v0.25 ship notes follow the v0.23/v0.24 pattern: paired McNemar on the synthesis fixture corpus is the ship gate, not LongMemEval.
evidence_preview: McNemar on synthesis corpus is ship gate

query: What is the right strike count for the resummerize exhaustion fuse?

recall_results.summary: v0.23.0-rc1 spec proposed a 5-strike exhaustion fuse counting any non-success outcome including LlmError and ClaimLost.
v0.23.0 ship pulled the strike count down to 3 after a Codex audit pointed out that 5 was too forgiving for genuine LLM-quality regressions.
v0.23.1 candidate kept the strike total at 3 but reclassified LlmError and ClaimLost as non-counting because they reflect transient or contention failure, not LLM quality.
Operator feedback after v0.23.1 candidate suggested 2 strikes would catch quality regressions faster; no decision logged yet.
evidence_preview: tighter fuse for faster regression catch

query: Should A1 operation registry use the proc-macro plus inventory pattern or static dispatch tables?

recall_results.summary: Original A1 spec compared a static dispatch table approach against the proc-macro plus inventory pattern; the spec chose the proc-macro path for single-author surface.
Phase 2 of A1 confirmed the proc-macro plus inventory pattern after benching the dispatch overhead at sub-microsecond per operation, well under the static-table alternative's compile-time cost.
Phase 3 deleted the old ops/registry.rs middleman entirely; the inventory iterator is now the single source of truth, removing any case for a parallel static table.
evidence_preview: inventory iterator is single source of truth

recall_results.summary: v0.22 D5 brainstorm revisited the question and re-affirmed the proc-macro path; bench showed p99 dispatch latency at 54 microseconds, far below any static-dispatch concern.

query: Are HDBSCAN clusters stable enough to be the load-bearing key for adaptive learning?

recall_results.summary: M4 spec asserts HDBSCAN clusters are stable enough across nightly reruns to serve as a per-memory tag for downstream learning.
An adaptive-engine devlog noted that HDBSCAN reassigns roughly 8 percent of memories per nightly run, which is borderline for downstream consumers that cache per-cluster statistics.
v0.7.1 closed the loop by making M2 alpha optimization and M3 survival decay tolerant to cluster reassignment via a smoothed exponential moving average per cluster.
evidence_preview: M2 and M3 tolerant to reassignment

recall_results.summary: Recent A1 dedup audit suggested per-cluster thresholds may need a coarser grouping than HDBSCAN provides; the matter is open.
evidence_preview: per-cluster dedup may need coarser grouping

query: What is the right keyword count for the synthesis fixture hit checker?

recall_results.summary: The original v0.23 resummerize fixture spec used 5 evidence_keywords with a top-5 frequency selection and 3-of-5 hit threshold for KeywordOverlapHitChecker.
v0.24 concept-summary fixtures inherited the 5-keyword convention; the score_concept_case helper enforces strict majority via hits*2 > n.
v0.25 synthesis fixtures locked the 5-keyword schema in a parse test that asserts every fixture has exactly 5 evidence_keywords.
An eval-team brainstorm proposed dropping to 3 keywords for tighter signal; the proposal was rejected because 3-of-3 leaves no buffer for keyword choice noise.
